record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Velickovic and Woodin proved that if A is a Σ^1_1 set with sup{ω_1^{CK(x)} : x ∈ A} = ω_1, then for every γ there exist x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3 in A such that γ ≤_h x_0 ⊕ x_1 ⊕ x_2 ⊕ x_3. Determine whether (a) there is a recursion-theoretic proof of this theorem, and (b) more generally, if A is a Σ^1_1(y) set and there is x ∈ A with ω_1^{CK(x)} > ω_1^{CK(y)}, must the Velickovic–Woodin conclusion hold for A?

evidence.quote: Theorem 8 (Velickovic–Woodin [2]). If A is Σ1_1 and sup{ωCK(x)_1 : x ∈ A} = ω1, then ∀γ∃x0, x1, x2, x3 ∈ A, γ ≤h x0 ⊕ x1 ⊕ x2 ⊕ x3.

Problem 9. (a) Is there a recursion theoretical proof for the above theorem of Velickovic–Woodin? (b) Is the following true: For any Σ1_1(y) set A, if there is x ∈ A such that ωCK(x)_1 > ωCK(y)_1, then the Velickovic–Woodin theorem holds for A?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in classical descriptive set theory and computability theory on Baire space. For a real $x \in \omega^\omega$, let $\omega_1^{CK(x)}$ denote the least ordinal that is not computable from $x$ (the Church–Kleene ordinal relative to $x$), and let $\omega_1$ denote the first uncountable ordinal. For reals $a,b$ write $a \leq_h b$ to mean that $a$ is hyperarithmetic in $b$, and let $a \oplus b$ denote the recursive join. Recall that a set $A \subseteq \omega^\omega$ is $\Sigma^1_1$ if it is the projection of a closed subset of $\omega^\omega \times \omega^\omega$, and $\Sigma^1_1(y)$ denotes the analogous class with parameter $y \in \omega^\omega$.

A theorem of Velickovic and Woodin asserts: if $A \subseteq \omega^\omega$ is $\Sigma^1_1$ and $\sup\{\omega_1^{CK(x)} : x \in A\} = \omega_1$, then for every countable ordinal $\gamma$ there exist $x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3 \in A$ such that $\gamma \leq_h x_0 \oplus x_1 \oplus x_2 \oplus x_3$ (i.e. a real coding $\gamma$ is hyperarithmetic in $x_0 \oplus x_1 \oplus x_2 \oplus x_3$).

Address the following two questions:

(a) Is there a purely recursion-theoretic (i.e. classical computability-theoretic, avoiding set-theoretic forcing or descriptive-set-theoretic large machinery) proof of this theorem?

(b) Does the following relativized strengthening hold: for every $y \in \omega^\omega$ and every $\Sigma^1_1(y)$ set $A \subseteq \omega^\omega$, if there exists some $x \in A$ with $\omega_1^{CK(x)} > \omega_1^{CK(y)}$, then for every ordinal $\gamma < \omega_1$ there exist $x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3 \in A$ with $\gamma \leq_h x_0 \oplus x_1 \oplus x_2 \oplus x_3$?

The problem is listed among open problems in computability theory and descriptive set theory, and no resolution was found in the available sources.
